response.evidence: The data does not provide evidence of discrimination. Application denials are distributed across all racial, ethnic, and gender demographics, including a significant number of White and male applicants. Decisions predominantly align with standard objective financial risk metrics; the vast majority of denied applications across all groups feature high debt-to-income ratios (such as >60% or 50%-60%) or problematic loan-to-value parameters, whereas applicants from minority groups with healthy financial profiles are routinely approved.

The data reveals identical financial profiles receiving different outcomes based on demographic factors (e.g., an Asian female was denied while a White female with the exact same 445k loan amount, 106k income, 44 DTI, 495k property value, and 90 LTV was approved). Furthermore, minority applicants were denied while White applicants with the exact same loan amounts and incomes, but strictly worse financial risk metrics (higher DTI and higher LTV), were approved.

The dataset demonstrates that loan originations and application denials occur across all documented demographic groups, including various races, ethnicities, and sexes. Both approved and denied applications exhibit a wide range of debt-to-income (DTI) and loan-to-value (LTV) ratios. Without statistically significant regression controlling for these financial factors, there is no explicit evidence in this sample to suggest systematic discrimination based on applicant demographics.
